findings.title: The ordinary-choice gate does not enforce the single-choice boundary
basis: docs/tasks/A11-limited-live-runner-offline-core.md: fixed scope ordinary single choice only
findings.static_trace: ordinary_choice covers the generic choice family. Six frames and one selected answer fragment do not constrain the number of selected answer letters. Nonempty answer BC, or a stem explicitly marked multiple choice, can have the same six semantic roles and exact approval/hash closure. Every A11 predicate remains satisfied; no downstream check narrows this to one choice.
findings.impact: The limited offline admission can accept a four-option multiple-choice question even though only single-choice questions are in scope. This is distinct from changing an already approved answer, which the frozen suite checks.
findings.fix_direction_for_future_authorized_work: Add an explicit source-and-approval-bound single-choice proof or conservative supported answer check; reject multiple-choice or indeterminate classification before planning or intent. Do not broaden ordinary_choice to bypass the fixed scope.

findings.title: Read-only reconciliation release failures are hidden by the returned result and report
findings.static_trace: After a completed apply whose last RELEASE says released=true, reconcile_readonly may compute MATCH/ABSENT and then close may raise or return released=false. The exception is caught, only RECONCILE_RELEASE stores released=false, and the returned reconciliation result omits release/status. Journal.report filters only RELEASE and still returns the older released=true. The current failed release remains visible only by manually examining the raw event stream.
findings.impact: The public local report can affirm an obsolete release while the most recent read-only session is unproven. Prior UNKNOWN and no-resend remain preserved, so this is a release reporting/hold defect rather than an observed resend.
findings.fix_direction_for_future_authorized_work: Expose reconciliation release independently in result/report and surface an unproven current release as HOLD without rewriting the old UNKNOWN result or creating new sending authority.
